chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the displacement that occurs in a limb, [stating that it is] one-third of the wergild of that limb.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّاقِلَةِ: Displacement or dislocation of a limb (specifically referring to the displacement of a bone from its joint)
key_terms.الْعُضْو: Limb or member of the body
key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for dislocating a bone in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, records Imam Ali’s (AS) judicial ruling on 'anqilabah' (dislocation), establishing the compensation as one-third of the full *diyah* for that limb. This specific valuation reflects the early Shia jurisprudential approach to quantifying bodily injuries, distinguishing between fractures and soft tissue or joint displacements. It serves as a foundational precedent in *fiqh al-jaraha* (law of injuries) for determining proportional compensation based on the severity of functional impairment.
